prize_parts.citation: for a visionary, densely patterned Romanian prose that makes memory, the body, dream and cosmology into an encyclopedic imaginative architecture, rooted in a poetic sensibility

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged after round 1, but I hold it with a narrower citation than before. On public knowledge, Cărtărescu's contribution is a sustained prose project with an unmistakable voice. The Blinding trilogy builds a deliberate structure from childhood memory, the body and dream. Solenoid reaches for the same material through a different frame, a diarist's account, and so appears to pursue the project by other means rather than repeat it. That is the best evidence I can offer on the chair's question about extension versus enlargement. It is a reading of how the major books relate to one another, not a verified close reading. The imaginative and intellectual depth, the formal ambition at the level of the whole book, and the personal rather than movement-dependent contribution remain the strongest combination on the shortlist under the common criteria. I would accept a citation limited to the major prose, since I cannot responsibly credit more than the novels I know. The poetic origin of the prose is a plausible but only partly tested premise, so I would carry it in the citation as a qualifying phrase and not as a separate claim about the poetry. This case rests on the work, not on reception, translation reach or national symbolism.
statement.case_against: The reservation I stated in round 1 stands and nothing in the exchange has resolved it. If the encyclopedic density of the longest books is experienced as unevenness and not architecture, the sustained-quality claim weakens, and I cannot rule that out from public knowledge or translation. I cannot judge the Romanian sentence, which is where the linguistic achievement lies. Olsson's point that the visionary-encyclopedic form has precedent in the novel is a serious test of formal risk, and I have not answered it beyond saying that the execution seems personal. Colleagues who prefer Michon or Zurita argue for a more concentrated intensity of language, and that argument may be right about where the sharpest sentence-level achievement lies. My preference rests on a weighting of breadth, architecture and depth against compression, not on a demonstrated superiority of the prose.

responses.point: Mattson keeps Michon first for sentence-level exactness and holds that a small, concentrated oeuvre is a feature and not a gap. She also doubts whether the scale and self-reference of Cărtărescu's late books sustain their length, and she asks that both writers be tested on the quality of the prose.
responses.response: I accept that smallness is not shallowness and that Michon's concentration is real. I rated him fourth for sentence-level achievement, not for lack of depth. Your doubt about Cărtărescu's length is the test I apply to my own preference, and I cannot dismiss it. I would still weigh the breadth criterion differently. Nobel's will asks about a whole body of work. A major achievement placed early and a narrow thematic field are harder to argue as sustained across that body, however exact the sentence. Your request to test both on the prose itself is fair, but it cannot be met from translations I cannot check for either writer. For that reason I would not let the committee treat my agreement on Michon's quality as a vote for him, nor your doubt about length as settled against Cărtărescu.

responses.point: Olsson keeps Zurita first for a radical formal conception and a voice sustained over decades. In round 1 he accepted that a citation can be limited to the poems, and he argues that Cărtărescu's encyclopedic cosmology rests on an established tradition and carries less formal risk.
responses.response: Your acceptance of a poems-only citation answers part of my round-1 objection. If the sequences themselves carry the case, the boundary problem for literary assessment is much smaller. It does not remove my other concern, which is that poetry in translation is the weakest ground for a judgment about voice and sustained quality. I have not read the printed sequences closely enough to move him above fifth on that basis. I take your point about tradition. The encyclopedic and visionary mode has precedents, and the question is whether Cărtărescu's handling of it is personal. I think it is, because the bodily, oneiric and autobiographical material gives the architecture its own logic. That is a judgment from public knowledge, and I would not claim it as demonstrated. Your own weakened-preference condition seems honest to me, and I would revise if poem-level evidence for Zurita were presented to the committee.

responses.point: Swärd keeps Can Xue first for a radical break with realist psychology and causality, held for decades. She argues that consistency of method is not by itself a lack of depth and that translation risk applies equally to Cărtărescu.
responses.response: I agree that consistency of method is not a flaw in itself, and I agree that translation risk does not separate your candidate from mine. I apply the same standard to both. Our difference is what the evidence lets us show. For Cărtărescu, the relation between the trilogy and Solenoid gives me something to point to when I say the work extends and does not repeat. For Can Xue, I have no comparable specific account of a later work that re-examines the earlier mode. I do not take that gap as a verdict against her, and I would welcome a specific later novel or story cycle where the method visibly transforms. Until then she stays my first alternative, ahead of Adonis, because her break with realist narrative is the most complete on the list. I do not move her above Cărtărescu.

responses.point: Palm also prefers Cărtărescu and asks that my qualification, whether density sustains quality across the long novels, stay in the record and not be hidden by the shared first place.
responses.response: I agree, and I have kept that qualification in my case against. Shared first place on our ballots says nothing about whether the longest books are controlled, and I do not treat it as evidence. The two of us rest on public knowledge and translation. If the committee decides the late books enlarge the project without deepening it, my preference would weaken, and I would want the next-best case, whichever it is, argued on specific works and not on who else supports it.

uncertainties: Whether the late, very long books extend the project or only enlarge it rests on my reading of how the major novels relate and is not verified by close reading.
The Romanian sentence, rhythm and density cannot be judged directly, so the linguistic achievement at the center of the case depends on translation.
The poetry and earlier short fiction are less well known to me, so the poetic grounding of the prose is only partly tested. I accept a citation limited to the major prose for that reason.

Comparative judgments among Cărtărescu, Michon, Zurita, Can Xue and Adonis cross languages and genres and depend on translations of uneven quality, notably for poetry. I apply one standard of translation risk to all candidates.

For Adonis, whether the later work sustains the earlier, more innovative phase remains unsettled, and Arabic prosody travels only partly in translation. I keep him as an alternative with limited confidence.
No source was independently verified and no text was freshly read for this stage. Support counts from round 1 are not treated as literary merit.
statement.conflict_note: No documented personal or professional tie to any shortlisted writer appears in the supplied profile. My own literary practice concerns Central Europe, and I have long ties to Prague and Vienna literary milieus and to the Dagens Nyheter and Svenska Dagbladet culture sections. I treat this as context only and not as evidence of a preference for a Romanian writer. I was elected to the Academy alongside Ingrid Carlberg, an ordinary collegial tie. Carlberg's committee voting status is undocumented and her simulated vote is a modeling assumption. Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
